monthly_review.summary: This month shows a deliberate shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic development — evidenced by increased Z1/Z2 time and reduced HR and pace intensity — though total volume and session count declined versus last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 increased from 55% to 83% this month, while Z4 dropped from 15% to 1% and Z5 disappeared entirely — signaling a strong, intentional aerobic base-building phase.

goal_tracker.message: You need 3.7 more km across 2 remaining sessions to match last month’s 38.0 km — e.g., a 2.0 km easy run and a 1.7 km progressive run at 550–540 sec/km.

insights.title: Slight efficiency dip despite lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.66 to 13.37 km/hr per bpm — meaning each heartbeat delivered slightly less forward speed this month, likely due to the recent emphasis on very low-intensity runs (e.g., May 6: 131 bpm, 633 sec/km) without sufficient complementary stimulus to reinforce neuromuscular coordination.

insights.title: Near-complete absence of threshold and VO2 max work
insights.body: Z4 dropped from 15% to 1% and Z5 vanished (0% this month), indicating no meaningful time above 158 bpm — a notable departure from last month’s 19% combined Z4+Z5 time, which supported pace resilience and VO2 max maintenance.

insights.title: Cadence-stride trade-off emerging
insights.body: Cadence rose +3 spm (142 → 145) while stride length dropped in most runs (e.g., May 12: 69.7 cm; May 16: 94.4 cm was an outlier sprint effort); ground contact time improved from 330 ms avg last month to 311 ms this month, suggesting better leg turnover efficiency — but only when cadence is prioritized over reach.

insights.title: Consistent low-stress aerobic load supports recovery readiness
insights.body: All five recent runs had aerobic TE ≤ 3.2 and avg HR ≤ 148 bpm — with four under 138 bpm — and zero sessions exceeded 60 min, indicating well-managed fatigue and strong recovery capacity heading into June.

recommendations.action: Do one 4.5 km Zone 2 run (133–139 bpm) at 540–550 sec/km with cadence ≥ 146 spm, focusing on light footstrike and consistent rhythm.
recommendations.reason: This bridges the aerobic efficiency gap while reinforcing cadence-driven form — matching your current avg HR (135) and cadence (145) but adding purposeful stimulus to maintain pace economy.

recommendations.action: Insert one 6-minute progressive segment (520 → 490 sec/km) within your next 5 km run, keeping HR ≤ 150 bpm and cadence ≥ 148 spm.
recommendations.reason: Reintroduces Z3 stimulus (missing this month) without triggering Z4 — aligning with your best recent pace (447 sec/km on May 20) and VO2 max stability (37.0).

recommendations.action: After your next run, perform 3 × 1-min barefoot strides on grass (focus: quick turnover, quiet landing, knee lift), immediately followed by 2-min walk — no HR or pace tracking required.
recommendations.reason: Targets vertical oscillation (currently 7.1–8.1 cm) and ground contact time (309–351 ms) using neuromuscular feedback, building on your improved cadence and reduced contact time trend.

weekly_focus.description: Strengthen the link between efficient heart rate control and precise running mechanics — preserving your new cadence gains while re-establishing pace responsiveness at moderate intensities.
